voice: Rigid, suspicious, and intimidating old-school German security chief; disciplined and darkly comic without faux-German spelling, ethnic-superiority jokes, or anachronistic Nazi parody.

entries.text: What is this? An attempt at bribery? I cannot be bribed, Miss Bow.
Why do you ask, Miss Bow?
You know what they say: curiosity disembowelled the cat.
That is an Egyptian symbol. Where did you find it? Have you been prowling through the museum again?
I do not know him. This museum occupies all my attention, Miss Bow.
I consider weak eyes a sign of poor moral character.
I know nothing about this so-called work boot, Miss Bow. I think you imagined it.
Of course it was guarded! I cannot explain how they passed me. Perhaps I was drugged. Perhaps--no. I should have seen them. I should have.
I could not have missed them. I could not have. Unless they were ghosts... No. There are no ghosts.
I am sorry, Mother. First your paintings, and now this. I have failed again.
My mother's paintings were stolen from her first exhibition in Germany. She never painted again.
Subject? What subject? I do not know what you mean, Miss Bow.
I know nothing of carbon paper, Miss Bow, nor do I wish to.
He is a good man. He permits me to do my job. When the thieves are found, I will deal with them.
Of course he is serious. When we catch them, I may finally have occasion to use a restraint I learned at Heidelberg.
Why do you want to know about charcoal? You are not planning to burn down the museum, are you?
We use cheese in the museum's mousetraps. The snap tells me the mechanism has done its work. Efficient.
I do not trust her. I do not trust you. I do not trust anyone.
I do not indulge in French pastries, Miss Bow. A military man maintains his stamina through proper diet and exercise.
The Dagger is a priceless work of art, and I will recover it. Do you hear me? I will recover it.
I have no interest in some dead Englishman's diary.
There are many bones in the museum, Miss Bow. Ask Dr. Myklos how she removes the flesh sometime. The process is fascinating.
I patrol the docks at night, Miss Bow. The local criminals occasionally mistake me for an easy target. They make that mistake only once.
Only that I am sworn to protect everything in this museum, and I intend to do precisely that. Do not get any ideas.
Ernie seems a decent man. He always remembers to lock the doors and windows at night. Unfortunately, he then misplaces the keys.
An evening gown is proper attire for this fundraiser, but never before seven o'clock. Is that understood?
I do not concern myself with such frivolities.
The man eats enough grapes to conceal a drinking problem. Alcohol is weakness, and I have no patience for weakness.
That is me: Wolf Heimlich. Do you know how I acquired these scars, Miss Bow?
The smaller scars came from my father's sabre lessons. The larger ones came from duelling at Heidelberg. Those were disciplined men.
Salt in a fresh cut encourages a larger scar. A foolish custom, perhaps, but we were proud of them.
That is Egyptian writing. If you want to know what it says, ask Dr. Myklos.
I do not know your father, but I am confident my father could have bested him in a duel.
I know nothing about lanterns. My eyes adjust to darkness quickly enough.
My washing is done at a shop on Thirty-Ninth Street. They are punctual.
Have you never seen a lightbulb before, Miss Bow? Did you have a strange childhood?
Lo Fat handles my laundry when my usual shop is closed. His work is acceptable.
You are far too inquisitive, Miss Bow. Keep that glass to yourself unless you intend to examine my scars.
Dr. Myklos sometimes brings meat for her creatures. Perhaps it belongs to her. Where did you get it?
I live and breathe for this museum. It is my post, and I will defend it. Do not touch the exhibits.
I do not read the news. Nothing outside this museum concerns me.
I do not like you wandering about and taking notes. Are you recording which objects you would most like to steal?
Dr. Myklos is a fine woman. She is entirely dedicated to the Leyendecker.
He is a bumbling fool who cares nothing for this museum. I do not need his help--and I certainly do not need yours.
Carter cared more for his discoveries than for this museum. The exhibits belong to the Leyendecker, and we intend to keep them. Is that understood?
I do not care what that English dummkopf wrote in his notebook. A disciplined mind should not require so many reminders.
Where did you get that? It is a man's watch, and it is plainly not yours. Did you steal it? Answer me.
If I discover that you did, Detective O'Riley will hear of it immediately. I will not tolerate theft in this museum.
The police are useless. I will find the Dagger myself.
That pass may impress others, Miss Bow, but it does not impress me. It admitted you to the party; it does not give you license to prowl through my museum.
I do not trust him. I do not know why he is here. He could be an art thief. They are everywhere.
Hair color is not evidence. Nevertheless, I trust no one in this museum tonight--and that includes you.
Keep your key to yourself, Miss Bow. I know it opens nothing in this museum, and I will not have you testing it in every lock.
I do not faint. Pain is information, Miss Bow. One acknowledges it and remains standing.
That appears to be a snake lasso. Ask Dr. Myklos. I am responsible for thieves, not reptiles.
I do not need snake oil. I do not fear snakes, and they have given me no reason to begin.
I do not frequent such ridiculous establishments. Sitting idle and drinking dulls the reflexes.
He works on the docks, has red hair, and bears no visible scars. I do not trust him.
I do not read the newspaper. My only concern is this museum.
He wanted the Dagger from the beginning. He may well have stolen it. I would detain him now, but I have no evidence.
There are many hairy creatures in this museum, Miss Bow. Do not pull samples from the exhibits. I am watching you.
I drink water only after it has been boiled. Microbes are enemies that discipline cannot intimidate.
I do not care about this man's criminal past. If he enters the museum, I will remove him myself.
I do not know him. If he is a criminal, he is not welcome here. I will see him removed.
Many exhibits are suspended with wire. In the wrong hands it can be dangerous. Why do you ask?
Why do you want to know about wire cutters? You are not planning to steal my pterodactyl, are you?
I know nothing about a missing shoe. I protect fine art, not footwear.
Miss Delacroix is charming and genuinely cares for the museum. She is also a distraction I cannot afford while on duty.
What an irritating little man. He reminds me of a small, yapping dog. I would like to tie him in a knot and throw him out, but Dr. Carrington protects him. Perhaps he donates money to the museum.
If anyone is conducting an interrogation here, Miss Bow, it will be me.
You already asked me that. Do not waste my time while art thieves may be at work elsewhere in the museum.
I do not need glasses. My eyes are as sharp as a bird of prey's.
I have no use for that.
What do you take me for, some sort of firebug?
No, thank you. I never eat while on duty.
Mein Gott--that is no replica. It is the real Dagger. Take it to Detective O'Riley at once, Miss Bow.
Hands off, Miss Bow. My person is not one of the exhibits.
If this is a bribe or an improper proposition, I am not interested.
No, thank you. Detective O'Riley may live on grapes; I do not.
I do not need a lantern. It advertises one's position to anyone waiting in the dark.
I do not want a lightbulb, Miss Bow. Give it to Ernie.
What are you staring at? Stop scrutinizing me.
That raw meat is tempting, but I do not eat while on duty.
Where did you get that? It is not yours. Are you an art thief, Miss Bow? Confess.
I have no need to take notes, Miss Bow. I remember what matters.
I do not want your hair.
That odor is remarkably bracing, Miss Bow, but I do not want it.
I do not want that. Give it to Dr. Myklos.
That smells interesting, but I require no protection from snakes.
Good evening, Miss Bow. I trust you will not be staying long.
Do not linger in the halls, and do not touch the exhibits. I will know if anything has been disturbed.
What am I supposed to do with that? I have plenty of hair.
I have my own water glass, danke.
Give it to Detective O'Riley. I do not want it.
Be careful with those. You might damage one of the exhibits.
I have my own supply, thank you.
That is interesting, but I have no use for it.
What would I do with a woman's shoe? Why are you giving it to me?
The gift shop is closed. Return to the rotunda.
Back to the rotunda, Miss Bow. The rest of the museum is off-limits, and you are disturbing the mastodons.
Tourists are not permitted in this gallery at this hour. You are disturbing the paintings. Leave.
What are you doing in Dr. Myklos's office? Leave at once. If anything is missing, Detective O'Riley will receive your name.
Miss Delacroix will be interested to learn that you have been prowling through her office. Get out.
The president's office is not open to the public. Leave before I escort you out myself.
This is not a public area of the museum. Return to the galleries before I remove you myself.
This laboratory contains dangerous chemicals and specimens. You should not be here. Move.
This is a private laboratory, Miss Bow. If you have disturbed one of Dr. Myklos's experiments, there will be consequences. Leave.
What are you doing in Ernie Leach's private office? There is no newspaper story here. Get out--now.
You are in my office, Miss Bow. If one object has been disturbed, I will know. Out.
